notes.title: internal_2 · ScaledCityWorld
notes.summary: Two pilots on 23 September, three runs in each condition: AABB flew the swarm first, AABC the single drone. The first run in each condition was practice, which leaves two counted runs per pilot and condition. The city was ScaledCityWorld, the city pack's tiles with every building a quarter as wide and 50 m tall. Answers were said aloud and entered after the session, so each run ends where the experimenter stopped the recording.

items: ScaledCityWorld replaces CityWorld: the pack's buildings at a quarter of their width and all 50 m tall, so the streets are wide and the skyline flat (287cf27e), with the streets widened further (a588d2fd).
The buildings are obstacles at last: in CityWorld they stood on the wrong layer, and the swarm's avoidance never saw them (287cf27e, d3cae643).
Goal patches with buildings twice as wide and a centre building (fa1b302f, 512f49fd), and an altitude ceiling 50 m above the ground (518f532e).

items: Each building avoided as a cylinder, damped and shielded (23e49a1e, eaffb2e1); a hollow core, so more drones stand on the formation's edge with their feeds shown (e0d9d30b); the gains retuned for flying through the city (1cb148ec).
A heading loop: each drone turns at its full 75 °/s, where a drag bug had held it near 35 °/s (37094462, 1f612c27), and a feed waits until its drone faces its heading (5ea29c90).

Three hats, a cowboy hat, a cap and a bucket hat, a different one at each goal (87138574, 21cfafe4), hung on the walker's head, with 8 walkers per patrol (38143432).

Answers said aloud and entered after the session from the experimenter's notes, matched to the goals in the order visited.

smoothness.title: How the pilot flew
smoothness.html: The stick measures are what this series was first analysed for: whether pilots hold one command and let the swarm find its way, or keep re-steering.

losses.title: Drones lost
losses.html: Nearly every loss was a pair of drones colliding at the tightest spread the dial allows (d_ref 0.4): the hollow core braked each ring drone by a different amount, and the lattice could not push a close pair apart hard enough. The next series flew the fix.

panorama.title: The stitched panorama
panorama.html: How long the stitched panorama was on screen in place of the three front feeds. These runs predate the recorder's panorama events: the editor log of the day records each switch, but not always when, so most of each run is unknown and the share is a wide range.

notes.reading:
In total the swarm was level with one drone for AABB and quicker for AABC, and neither the goals nor the way between them separate the two conditions.

AABC flew the swarm second, so its lead is also a lead of practice; AABB, who flew the swarm first, was level. The clearest difference is in how the pilots flew: AABC steered the swarm far less than the single drone (less stick movement, fewer adjustments, much less turning), AABB more. Both of AABB's counted swarm runs lost drones to collisions at the tightest spread (d_ref 0.4), the failure the next series' damper was built for; AABC's did not.
data_notes: The first run of each pilot in each condition was practice (test.json): drawn, counted in no summary.
The answers were entered after the session, so no run records when a hat was named: the total time ends where the experimenter stopped the recording, at the last answer said aloud.
The task is timed from the start line, found in the drone logs; the series itself was timed from Play.
Drone losses are attributed from the editor log kept that day.
